newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar trapped in ranges as NY subdued.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar trapped in ranges as NY subdued.

text.p: White sugar futures stayed trapped in their earlier tight ranges on Friday afternoon, reflecting the general lack of activity on the New York market, traders said.
July raws were pinioned between 10.77 and 10.88 cents/lb, ensuring that producer stops remained untriggered. Traders have said sell and buy stops are broadly placed at 10.60 and 10.90 respectively.
August-based spread trading was the main focus of activity in London as the benchmark August/October widened further to around $10.00 from the $9.00 seen earlier in the session, they said.
Price movements were tight across the board, as were trading ranges. One leading trade house was said to be a good buyer of August-based spreads and light broker buying was cited in August/March.
At 1555 GMT August was up 70 cents at $313.00, close to its intraday high of $313.20. October was down 70 cents at $303.00 and volume reached a light 1,174 lots.
"The (London) market does feel steady and like it's going to creep higher," one trader said.
Thursday's public holiday across much of Europe had prompted many players to take long weekends, he added.
Other market sources said the gradual upturn in physical demand should keep August whites supported above $310.00 and cause spreads to widen down the board.
"People are beginning to think that maybe the whites haven't got a great deal more on the downside, but it's not exactly rushing to the upside," said one.
"The August/October spread is reflecting some of the interest, that's beginning to strengthen -- but at some stage it will have a drag effect, especially the October/December."
